**Samsung Galaxy Store:** One MCP server, App Store Publisher MCP, lets AI agents publish Android apps to Samsung Galaxy Store and Huawei AppGallery. It has tools for uploading binaries, updating listings, submitting apps, and verifying Samsung IAP receipts. Access requires a Samsung Seller Portal service account, and that requires commercial seller status.

**Huawei AppGallery:** A separate project, huawei-app-gallery-mcp on PyPI, can manage localized store listings per language and upload APK/AAB files, with automatic chunked upload for large files.

**Google Play and App Store Connect:** The app-publish-mcp project covers both App Store Connect and Google Play Console, with 91 tools for listings, screenshots, releases, reviews & submissions. The search turned up several open-source MCP servers that cover parts of this workflow, though none clearly does all of it (privacy policy handling is the thinnest area).

- **fastlane-mcp (pampas93):** A local MCP server that wraps Gradle and fastlane so coding agents can publish to Google Play and App Store Connect. It covers Android metadata, screenshots, images, and changelogs, plus iOS privacy details and age rating config. It does not create the Play app listing itself, so you need to set that up first.
- **app-publisher-mcp (seungmanchoi):** Its tools include writing listing text to fastlane metadata files and publishing to Google Play through fastlane. It also generates privacy-policy content. Age ratings and App Privacy settings must still be configured in App Store Connect, since fastlane does not support uploading them.
- **google-play-mcp (roadhero):** A self-described independent, open-source MCP server for Google Play operations. Its first release is read-only, with no publish, refund, delete or permission-changing tools. It is not an official Google product.
- **play-console-mcp (taimweromita505):** A hosted Cloudflare Worker that is still in developer beta, with publishing disabled. Text listings are supported, but screenshots, graphics, app creation, and financial reports are not included.
- **google-play-store-mcp (Clueless-Creations, via Glama):** Focused on listing metadata, reading fastlane/supply-style directories, and staging edits without committing them.
- **google-play-console-mcp (PyPI):** Advertises 170 tools, including screenshots and store assets, with a confirmation gate on destructive writes.

On the Play side, fastlane's supply tool covers the screenshot and metadata upload. Its docs say you need to set up your app manually first by uploading at least one build, and it offers a validate-only option.

I didn't find a dedicated open-source MCP server that handles the privacy policy itself (hosting, linking, or Data safety form answers). The closest matches only generate or populate privacy-policy text. Also, screenshot requirements, such as no alpha channel, apply on top of any tool you use.

content.content:
**App Publisher MCP** is an MCP server for generating app icons and store assets, preparing store listings, and publishing to app stores.

## Features

- **Icons:** Generates icons with Google Gemini, then resizes them for iOS (15 sizes plus `Contents.json`) and Android (6 densities plus a 512x512 Play Store icon).
- **Screenshots:** `generate_screenshot` creates mockups. `maestro_store_screenshot` captures from a running simulator or emulator and adds AI headlines and device frames at store sizes.
- **Feature graphics:** The page doesn't describe generating these. It only lists `playstore_upload_image`, which uploads icons, screenshots, or feature graphics.
- **Privacy policy:** `generate_store_listing` drafts privacy policy content for iOS and Android.
- **Age rating:** Auto-detects app capabilities and produces answers for the iOS age rating questionnaire, plus a content rating guide for Android.
- **Ads detection:** The App Privacy guide detects data collection from dependencies such as AdMob. AdMob tools can also create ad units and generate React Native integration code, though creating apps and ad units may be restricted by Google.
- **Google Play upload:** `publish_android` uses fastlane, and the Play Store tools manage listings, tracks, and images through the API.
- **Fastlane format:** `setup_fastlane` creates the Fastfile, Appfile, and metadata structure. `populate_metadata` and `validate_metadata` manage the metadata files.
- **Other stores:** The page covers only the Apple App Store and Google Play.

## License

MIT

## Install

Requires Node.js. Fastlane is needed for publishing, and Java 17+ is needed for Maestro. You also need a Gemini API key.

```
claude mcp add app-publisher -- npx @seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp
```

Or with environment variables:

```
claude mcp add app-publisher \
  -e GEMINI_API_KEY=your_api_key_here \
  -e GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash-image \
  -- npx @seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp
```

Restart Claude Code after adding the server.

## MCP Client Config

Add this to `~/.claude.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "app-publisher": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "GEMINI_API_KEY": "your_api_key_here",
        "GEMINI_MODEL": "gemini-2.5-flash-image"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## fastlane-mcp 0.2.2: Summary

**Features**
- Builds iOS and Android apps with different configurations
- Deploys to AppCenter and Firebase App Distribution
- Runs automated tests on devices and simulators
- Handles iOS code signing certificates and provisioning profiles
- Bumps version and build numbers
- Uploads app store metadata and screenshots
- Lists available Fastlane lanes in a project

**Tools:** `fastlane_build`, `fastlane_test`, `fastlane_deploy`, `fastlane_list_lanes`, `fastlane_match`, `fastlane_version`

**License:** MIT

**Install**
- From PyPI: `pip install fastlane-mcp`
- From source: clone the repository, then run `uv sync`
- Run the server: `uv run python -m fastlane_mcp.server` or `uv run fastmcp run src/fastlane_mcp/server.py`

**Configuration**

Environment variables:
- `FASTLANE_USER`: Apple ID for iOS builds
- `FASTLANE_PASSWORD`: App-specific password
- `APPCENTER_API_TOKEN`: AppCenter API token
- `FIREBASE_TOKEN`: Firebase CI token
- `MATCH_PASSWORD`: Password for match certificates

The page also gives MCP client examples for Claude Desktop and Cursor, which set the command, arguments, working directory, and environment variables in a JSON config file.

**Requirements**
- Python 3.11 or later (the classifiers list 3.11 and 3.12)
- Fastlane installed and configured for your projects
- iOS: Xcode and an Apple Developer account
- Android: Android SDK and Java
- Firebase CLI (for Firebase features)
- AppCenter CLI (for AppCenter deployment)

**Limitations (manual steps)**

The page doesn't have a formal limitations section, but it implies these manual steps:
- Install Fastlane yourself (for example, `gem install fastlane`)
- Set up Fastlane Match for iOS certificate management
- Log in to the Firebase CLI (`firebase login`)
- Set the `APPCENTER_API_TOKEN` variable yourself
- Keep credentials in environment variables, not in version control, and use an app-specific password for Apple ID authentication
- Install Xcode, the Android SDK, Java, and the Firebase and AppCenter CLIs before using the related features

The page also says the release has no provenance metadata, and the project is marked "4 - Beta."

**App Store Publisher MCP** is an MCP server for publishing Android apps to Samsung Galaxy Store and Huawei AppGallery from AI agents.

**License:** MIT, © Alvin Ahmad

**Features**
- **Samsung Galaxy Store:** app list and details, arbitrary Seller API calls, and JWT service-account auth.
- **Huawei AppGallery:** app ID lookup, app info, file upload URLs, and submission, with three credential types supported.
- **Samsung IAP:** verification of purchase receipt JWTs against your public key.
- Tokens are cached and auto-refreshed, and credentials stay in a local `.env` file.

**Install**
```
git clone https://github.com/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp.git
cd app-store-publisher-mcp
npm install
cp .env.example .env
```
For Claude Code:
```
claude mcp add app-store-publisher -- node /path/to/app-store-publisher-mcp/index.js
```
Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Google Antigravity, and OpenCode each use a JSON config entry pointing to `index.js`.

**Requirements**
- Node.js and npm. The page doesn't state a specific version.
- **Samsung:** a Seller Portal service account (requires commercial seller status), providing `SAMSUNG_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID` and `SAMSUNG_PRIVATE_KEY`.
- **Huawei:** a Connect API client created with Project = N/A, providing `APPGALLERY_CLIENT_ID` and `APPGALLERY_CLIENT_SECRET`. A service-account key JSON and API key are optional.

**GitHub:** https://github.com/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp

**License:** MIT. The page says only "MIT" under the License section and does not link a license file.

**Google Play questions**

- **First manual upload:** The page doesn't say whether you must upload a first AAB by hand. It does say that "The first release of a new app still requires manual setup in App Store Connect or Play Console," including "policy, privacy, or content declarations." For an existing, fully configured Android app, "a signed AAB is usually enough to let the MCP run the update workflow."
- **Data safety:** The server has a `google_update_data_safety` tool. The page doesn't say whether the initial Data safety form must be completed manually.
- **Content rating:** The page doesn't mention content rating or an MCP tool for it. It falls under the "content declarations" manual setup, but the page doesn't say so explicitly.

**Install**

From the repository:

```
npm install
npm run build
```

The page also links an npm package named `app-publish-mcp`, but it doesn't give a global install command.

**Configuration**

- Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set the Apple variables (`APPLE_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_KEY_TYPE`, `APPLE_ISSUER_ID`, `APPLE_P8_PATH`) and the Google variable `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH`.
- For Google, you can use a service account or OAuth. For OAuth, run `app-publish-mcp auth google --client-id=... --client-secret=...`, or set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN`.
- To add it to Claude Code, put an `mcpServers` entry in `~/.claude/settings.local.json` that runs `node` on `dist/index.js` with the environment variables.
- Set `APP_PUBLISH_READ_ONLY=true` to register only read-oriented tools.

**Fastlane metadata:** The page doesn't mention fastlane, so I can't say whether the server reads or writes fastlane metadata.

- Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and set the Apple variables (`APPLE_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_KEY_TYPE`, `APPLE_ISSUER_ID`, `APPLE_P8_PATH`) and the Google variable `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH`.
- For Google, you can use a service account or OAuth. For OAuth, run `app-publish-mcp auth google --client-id=... --client-secret=...`, or set `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, and `GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN`.
- To add it to Claude Code, put an `mcpServers` entry in `~/.claude/settings.local.json` that runs `node` on `dist/index.js` with the environment variables.
- Set `APP_PUBLISH_READ_ONLY=true` to register only read-oriented tools.

**Fastlane metadata:** The page doesn't mention fastlane, so I can't say whether the server reads or writes fastlane metadata.

content.text:
I didn't find one open-source MCP server that does everything on your list. My recommendation is a small stack built on fastlane-format metadata:

1. **Core: [`app-publisher-mcp`](https://github.com/seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp)** (MIT, npm). It comes closest to what you asked for:
   - **Icons:** generates them with Gemini and exports every Android size plus the 512×512 Play icon.
   - **Screenshots:** captures them from a running emulator using Maestro, then adds device frames and headlines.
   - **Privacy policy:** drafts one with `generate_store_listing`.
   - **Content rating:** auto-detects what the app does and gives you an Android content-rating guide.
   - **Ads and data collection:** finds them from your dependencies (for example AdMob).
   - **Metadata:** writes and validates it in the fastlane format.
   - **Publishing:** uploads to Google Play through fastlane `supply` and the Play API.
2. **Samsung Galaxy Store (and Huawei): [`app-store-publisher-mcp`](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp)** (MIT). You need a Samsung Seller Portal service account, and that requires **commercial seller status**.
3. **F-Droid: you don't need an MCP server.** F-Droid doesn't accept uploaded APKs. It builds your app from source after you open a merge request to `fdroiddata`. It reads `fastlane/metadata/android/` straight from your repo, so the same metadata covers it.
4. **Optional, for more Play API coverage: [`app-publish-mcp`](https://github.com/maksym-kyryliuk/app-publish-mcp)** (MIT, 91 tools). It includes a Data safety tool, release tracks and review management. Its docs don't mention fastlane.

**Don't use for publishing:** `roadhero/google-play-mcp` is read-only for now, and `play-console-mcp` has publishing turned off.

## What still needs you (no tool gets around these)
- **First-time Play setup:** You have to create the app in Play Console yourself, and `supply` needs at least one build uploaded manually first.
- **Play Console forms:** The content-rating (IARC) questionnaire and the ads and target-audience declarations aren't fully available through the API. The MCP can work out the answers, but you click them in once, which takes about 10 minutes. After that, updates run automatically.
- **New personal developer accounts:** Google requires a closed test with 12 testers for 14 days before production.
- **Privacy policy hosting:** It needs a public URL. GitHub Pages works and is free.
- **"Free" caveat:** Image generation uses a Gemini API key. There's a free tier, but image models may need billing turned on.
- **"Auto-fix on failure":** No server does this. The agent does it: Claude Code reads the `supply` or API error, fixes the metadata or image, and runs it again. Use `supply --validate_only` for dry runs.

## Install
Assumptions: you're on macOS with Claude Code as the MCP client, and the app is a Gradle Android project.

```bash
# Prerequisites
brew install node fastlane openjdk@17      # plus Android SDK/adb (Android Studio)
curl -Ls "https://get.maestro.mobile.dev" | bash

# Core server
claude mcp add app-publisher \
  -e GEMINI_API_KEY=YOUR_KEY -e GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash-image \
  -- npx @seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp

# Samsung/Huawei (optional)
git clone https://github.com/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp.git
cd app-store-publisher-mcp && npm install && cp .env.example .env   # set SAMSUNG_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID, SAMSUNG_PRIVATE_KEY
claude mcp add app-store-publisher -- node "$PWD/index.js"
```

For Google Play:
1. In Google Cloud, create a service account and download its JSON key.
2. In Play Console, go to Users & permissions and invite that account.
3. Set `json_key_file` in `fastlane/Appfile`.

## First run
1. Create the app in Play Console. Upload a signed AAB to the internal testing track by hand once.
2. Start an emulator with the app installed, open Claude Code in the project folder, and ask:
   > "Set up fastlane for this project, generate a missing icon and feature graphic, capture store screenshots with Maestro, write the listing and a privacy policy based on the app's actual network calls, SDKs and permissions, tell me the content-rating and Data safety answers, then validate the metadata."
3. Check the privacy policy and rating answers, publish the policy on GitHub Pages, and fill in the Play Console forms once.
4. Ask the agent to "publish to the internal track," then promote the release to production when it looks right.
5. For F-Droid, commit `fastlane/metadata/android/` to your repo and open an MR to `gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroiddata`. You can check the recipe locally first with `fdroid lint` and `fdroid build`.

Note that some of these projects are young, so read each one's README before giving it your Play credentials.

Sources:
- [seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp](https://github.com/seungmanchoi/app-publisher-mcp)
- [App Store Publisher MCP (Glama)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/qalvinahmad/app-store-publisher-mcp)
- [maksym-kyryliuk/app-publish-mcp](https://github.com/maksym-kyryliuk/app-publish-mcp)
- [roadhero/google-play-mcp](https://github.com/roadhero/google-play-mcp)
- [play-console-mcp](https://github.com/taimweromita505-source/play-console-mcp)
- [fastlane-mcp (PyPI)](https://pypi.org/project/fastlane-mcp/)
- [fastlane upload_to_play_store docs](https://docs.fastlane.tools/actions/upload_to_play_store/)
- [F-Droid forum: submitting an app](https://forum.f-droid.org/t/i-want-to-upload-my-android-app-on-this-store/16908)
- [F-Droid forum: how to publish](https://forum.f-droid.org/t/how-to-publish-my-app-on-f-droid/198)
